A pooled parallel-query worker never has an identity: thread_entry_task.cpp:75-76 retire_context() sets private_lru_index = -1 and m_is_private_lru_enabled = false, :95 recycle_context() repeats it, and px_scan_task.cpp:94 propagates m_px_orig_thread_entry = m_parent_thread_p from the parent AND NOTHING ELSE. Only session.c:740 and server_support.c:2401,2437 ever assign one - i.e. the client transaction thread that serves a NO_PARALLEL_SCAN scan. PostgreSQL contrast: heapam.c:398-410 initscan() sets BAS_BULKREAD from rs_nblocks > NBuffers/4, :1340 sets SO_ALLOW_STRAT so each worker's own heap_beginscan builds its own 256 kB ring (freelist.c:426,442), and GetBufferFromRing/AddBufferToRing (:623,:702) recycle only pages the scan itself read - DOP-independent by construction, and StrategyGetBuffer (:184) is 1.73% of PostgreSQL's Q06 profile so the ring is provably active. Effect: 458,209 -> 158,930 reads/statement, -4.57 GiB of page-cache traffic, worth about 1.66 core-s of the 14.023 core-s excess (11.8%), independently bounded by CUBRID's measured 2.500 core-s parallel CPU inflation of which this is 66%. headline_finding: The headline ratio is not the finding. Before Q11 could be measured at all, CUBRID had to be driven through a 2.6408x performance decay that no parameter, plan or query change causes and that SSOT section 12's WARM gate cannot detect: block median 3.544000 -> 1.342000 s while physical page reads per statement fell 566,103 -> 0, with the plan, the query text, every parameter and the page-FIX count all held constant (trace `fetch` 1,012,042 -> 1,012,172 -> 1,011,949, a 0.02% spread). 94.9% of the 1,828 ms recovered is accounted for by the trace's own fetch_time (2,061 -> 528 -> 326 ms). PostgreSQL's number moved 0.01% over the same 22 minutes and ~370 statements: `Buffers: shared hit=676275 read=0` and Execution Time 1079.898 -> 1080.016 ms in three EXPLAIN ANALYZE captures. Two probes separate the variable: ONE connection running 120 statements is FLAT (2.450-2.521 s, half-split trend -0.16%, syscr 193,235-210,348, device read_bytes 0 over 379.9 GiB of rchar), while 60 connections x 4 statements decays 49,292 -> 34,538 -> 18,306 -> 3,519 -> 135 reads/statement over five connections and then holds 111-127 for 55 more, wall 1.581 -> 1.318-1.370 s; and one connection x 60 statements immediately afterwards is FLAT at the new level (median 1.3300 s, spread 2.28%, 96 reads/statement). The decay is CONNECTION-driven. Num_data_page_private_count sits at 5,002 for exactly as long as the misses persist - i.e. at PGBUF_PRIVATE_LRU_MAX_HARD_QUOTA = 5000 (page_buffer.c:1024) - and Num_data_page_lru1 (the shared hot zone) rises 15,092 -> 82,352 -> 97,369, which is Q11's whole working set, when they stop. A single session retains 5,000 of 524,288 pages, 0.95% of an 8,192 MB pool, for a working set that is 18.6% of it.

plan_comparison_summary: The two plans are closer than in any previous query of this campaign, and the join subtree is node-for-node identical. CUBRID (estimated, SET OPTIMIZATION LEVEL 514): temp(order by) <- temp(group by) sort 1 asc <- idx-join <- [idx-join <- sscan nation sargs n_name='GERMANY' + iscan supplier index fk_supplier_nation] + iscan partsupp index fk_partsupp_supplier, cost 6892 for the join and 9752 total, final cardinality estimate 320,000 against a true 323,920 (0.9879x - the most accurate estimate CUBRID has produced in this campaign); plus a structurally IDENTICAL second plan for the uncorrelated HAVING subquery. PostgreSQL (EXPLAIN ANALYZE): Sort <- HashAggregate (Planned Partitions 16, Batches 17, Memory Usage 8337kB, Disk Usage 15064kB, Rows Removed by Filter 296089) <- Nested Loop <- [Nested Loop <- Seq Scan nation Filter + Bitmap Heap Scan supplier on idx_fk_supplier_nation, Heap Blocks exact=1872] + Index Scan idx_fk_partsupp_supplier Index Searches 4049 loops=4049; plus InitPlan expr_1 -> Finalize Aggregate -> Gather (Workers Planned 1, Launched 1) -> Partial Aggregate -> Nested Loop <- Hash Join(supplier Parallel Seq Scan of all 100,000 rows, nation) + Index Scan idx_fk_partsupp_supplier. Buffers: shared hit=676275, temp read=1330 written=3103. Same: the nation filter (25 read, 1 kept), the supplier access (4,049 rows through the same FK index, 1 index search each side), the partsupp access (4,049 index searches, 323,920 rows, same index), and the whole cardinality chain 25 -> 1 -> 4,049 -> 323,920 -> 304,774 -> 8,685 which both engines independently confirm. Different: (1) the aggregation - CUBRID sorts (GROUPBY hash: partial, sort: true, 1,516 sort pages, SERIAL, 313 ms), PostgreSQL hashes and spills 17 batches (~200 ms) - and PostgreSQL's choice is the slower one; (2) the HAVING subquery - CUBRID runs SUBQUERY (uncorrelated) as a serial second copy of the whole join in 619 ms of a 1,532 ms statement (40.4%), PostgreSQL runs the same subquery under a Gather with 1 worker in 237 ms and reaches all 100,000 supplier rows with a Parallel Seq Scan instead of an index probe; (3) the join -> aggregation hand-off - CUBRID materialises the 323,920-row result into a temp list file and re-reads it, PostgreSQL passes TupleTableSlots by reference. Variants measured through the same gated section-12 block: CUBRID /*+ NO_HASH_AGGREGATE */ 1.340000 s (identical plan tree cost 9752, identical fetch 1,011,949, hash: partial -> hash: false, still no parallel workers); PostgreSQL enable_hashagg=off 0.739912 s (GroupAggregate over Sort, external merge Disk 8248kB); PostgreSQL max_parallel_workers_per_gather=0 0.870872 s (InitPlan Gather -> plain Aggregate, 237 -> 316.9 ms).
